stem: A client is scheduled for elective surgery on the left eye. During preprocedure verification, the nurse notes that no procedure-site mark is present. The client is alert and able to participate. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Proceed because eye surgery does not require site marking when the consent names the correct eye
options.B: Pause progression and ensure the licensed practitioner accountable for the procedure completes the required site-marking process before the procedure
options.C: Mark the left eye independently so the operating schedule is not delayed
options.D: Proceed to the final time-out because the time-out replaces site marking for paired organs

rationale: Joint Commission site-marking requirements apply when more than one possible procedural location exists and an incorrect site would affect safety or quality; eye surgery is specifically listed as a common example. The site is marked before the procedure by the licensed practitioner ultimately accountable for and present at the procedure, with the patient involved whenever possible. The nurse should therefore pause progression and ensure the required process is completed rather than independently marking outside the defined process or treating the time-out as a substitute.
educational_objective: For a lateralized procedure such as eye surgery, verify that required site marking is completed by the appropriately accountable licensed practitioner before the procedure and involve the patient whenever possible.
source_document_title: Universal Protocol – Site Marking: What are Joint Commission’s site marking requirements for operative or other procedures?
source_locator: Standards FAQ — Universal Protocol – Site Marking: minimum conditions requiring site marking; eye surgery example; accountable licensed practitioner; completion prior to procedure; patient involvement whenever possible
source_claim_supported: Joint Commission requires site marking for procedures with multiple possible locations when wrong-site performance would affect safety/quality, lists eye surgery as an example, and specifies who marks the site and when.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — protect client from injury; properly identify client; verify appropriateness and accuracy of treatment/procedure information, printed p. 24 (PDF page 27)
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — wrong-site procedure prevention
correction_summary: Replaced Universal Protocol component memorization with a current 2026 site-marking safety scenario. Kept the nurse within verification/escalation scope and separated this construct from the final-time-out discrepancy item Q1345.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current Joint Commission site-marking FAQ first published March 2026 verified directly.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Laterality requirement, eye-surgery example, responsible marker, timing and patient involvement are directly supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; eye surgery is specifically listed among procedures commonly requiring site marking.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; pauses care and ensures the accountable practitioner completes required marking.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; the nurse should not independently substitute for the defined accountable practitioner absent a permitted delegated arrangement.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; final time-out is complementary and does not replace required site marking.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B follows the specified Universal Protocol process under the stem conditions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are plausible workflow responses.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked delegation exceptions, patient refusal/not-feasible exceptions, emergency exceptions, and whether eye procedures are explicitly covered; stem excludes exceptions and B remains uniquely best.
